analysis:
This batch contains documentation only: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/ssd-ledger-charge-per-donation.md lines 1-13) and an edit to docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (head lines 393-400, plus the date at line 3). Both describe a write-budget change in SSDWriteBehind.chargeWholeDonation. An attention donation of several blocks now reserves their summed DBK3 size in one durable ledger charge before its first write. If that charge is refused (near the cap or under ledger contention), each block is charged before its own write. Blocks skipped after the whole-donation charge stay charged.

Security-relevant invariants the docs say are preserved:
- Charges precede writes.
- Charges are never refunded.
- The ledger holds only time buckets and byte counts.
- Corrupt or inaccessible accounting fails closed.

This is a wear and availability control, not a confidentiality control. Within T-041 it is one of the endurance guards; it does not affect HMAC naming, DBK3 AAD, TTL or salt scoping. Over-charging skipped blocks is conservative, meaning it fails toward fewer writes. A single large reservation could transiently consume budget other models would otherwise use. The changelog reports that cross-model refusals fell from 49% to 10%, so this is not a regression.

No source code for SSDWriteBehind.swift or SSDWriteBudget.swift was supplied, so I could not verify the following:
- the reservation is computed from the full serialized DBK3 sizes;
- the per-block fallback still charges each block before writing it;
- no path writes a block without a charge after a partially refused donation;
- the summed-size arithmetic cannot overflow;
- the cap check is still atomic across concurrent stores.

These are coverage limits for the integration pass, not evidence of safety. The threat model's T-041 posture needs no update from these documentation changes.
